title: Normal components after etale pullback
statement:
Let $W\to Y$ be etale with $W$ Noetherian and $Y$
normal integral.
Then $W$ is a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed
normal integral schemes.

proof.text: Let $w\in W$ with image $y\in Y$, and choose affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$ containing $y$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq W$ containing $w$ and mapping into $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The restriction $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] (being locally of finite presentation, flat and unramified are local on the source and target). Since $Y$ is normal in the sense of [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], every localization $A_{\mathfrak p}=\mathcal O_{Y,y'}$ is a normal domain, so $A$ is a normal ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal], $B$ is a normal ring, so $\mathcal O_{W,w}=B_{\mathfrak q}$ is a normal domain. Thus every local ring of $W$ is a normal domain; in particular $W$ is reduced.

Because $W$ is Noetherian, it has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finite-components]. Two distinct irreducible components cannot meet: at a point in their intersection, the local ring would have two distinct minimal primes, contradicting that it is a domain. Therefore the components are pairwise disjoint. Each irreducible component is closed, and the finite union of the other components is closed, so its complement is open; hence every component is open-and-closed. The local rings on a component are the corresponding local rings of $W$, so each component is normal; it is integral because it is irreducible and reduced, in the sense of [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois].

lean.statement: theorem Etale.exists_clopen_normal_integral_components {W Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : W ⟶ Y) [Etale f] [IsNoetherian W] (hY : IsNormalScheme Y) : ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → W.Opens), (∀ i, IsClosed (U i : Set W)) ∧ (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (U i) (U j)) ∧ (⨆ i, U i) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ i, IsNormalScheme (U i).toScheme)
